# Nexus Clip
> GNOME Shell 45–51 extension: Nexus has its own clipboard (LIFO stack + FIFO of prompts), user-defined shortcuts with per-shortcut prompts, and inference over an OpenAI-compatible /v1 endpoint. The system clipboard is touched only by explicit import/export.

## Core files
- extension/extension.js — Extension subclass; dynamic keybinding slots from the `shortcuts` list
- extension/lib/actions.js — orchestration: import/process/export/enqueue/run-next/drain/pop/HUD
- extension/lib/shortcuts.js — PURE: modes, canonical accelerators, defaults, migration, validation
- extension/lib/config.js — GSettings glue: load/save shortcuts, signature, API config
- extension/lib/hud.js — in-shell St/Clutter visual history (tabs Pilha/Histórico/Fila/Prompts, search) + live streaming panel + transient status chip (no GTK)
- extension/lib/prompts.js — PURE: built-in prompt template library + search
- extension/lib/history-core.js — PURE: parse/filter the append-only history.jsonl (newest-first, sanitized)
- extension/lib/notify-policy.js — PURE: notification policy (errors/all/silent) + status formatting
- extension/lib/command-keys.js — PURE: Super command palette map + queue badge/header formatting
- extension/lib/v1client.js — HTTP client: chat() (non-stream) + stream() (SSE), cancellable/timeout
- extension/lib/v1core.js — PURE: buildMessages/buildPayload/parseCompletion
- extension/lib/sse.js — PURE: SSE parser + incremental UTF-8 decoder
- extension/lib/store-core.js — PURE: LIFO/FIFO semantics, node shape, schemaVersion
- extension/lib/store-io.js — shared serialization over an injected file adapter
- extension/lib/store.js — GJS/Gio adapter (shell + prefs)
- tests/helpers/store-node.js — Node fs adapter (tests)
- extension/prefs.js — preferences: API / shortcuts (key capture + prompts) / Nexus / help
- extension/schemas/org.gnome.shell.extensions.nexus-clip.gschema.xml — GSettings schema
- docs/ARCHITECTURE.md — architecture, flows, state model, HTTP contract
- docs/USER_GUIDE.md — actions, shortcuts, import/export, queue, and HUD usage
- docs/CONFIGURATION.md — API settings, shortcut schema, GSettings, and local data files
- docs/DEVELOPMENT.md — build/install/test/smoke workflow
- docs/CRITICAL_POINTS.md — invariants (freeze, clipboard boundary, state) mapped to tests
- docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md — failure modes (including the old Super+X freeze)
- docs/adr/ — decision log (0001..0012)
- tests/ — node --test (logic + shell/schema contracts) + GJS store/client smoke scripts
- .githooks/ — pre-commit/pre-push run `make check` (enable with `make hooks`)
- .github/workflows/ci.yml — `make check` on pull requests and master

## Defaults
- `Super+;` — one global leader → keyboard command bar: C/V/X/Q/N/D/Z/H actions, 1–5 enqueue prompt templates; plain Super+letter stays natural.
- Motor memory: C=collect (system → Nexus), V=write (AI on Nexus top), X=move a copy out (Nexus → system); desktop Ctrl+C/V/X is never grabbed.
- `queue-badge=true` — persistent top badge with FIFO depth + next step while work is pending; disappears when empty.
- `<Alt><Super>c` — coletar: system clipboard → Nexus stack → prompt (borrowed from FIFO) → result node.
- `<Alt><Super>v` — escrever/processar: FIFO prompt applied to the Nexus top → new result node.
- `queue-auto=true` — serialize inference in a FIFO; `fifo.json` is the prompt queue, in-memory pipeline is the execution queue; session cache serves repeated pairs.
- `<Alt><Super>x` — mover/exportar: export a copy of the Nexus top to the system clipboard.
- `<Alt><Super>h` — history: open the visual history panel.
- `<Alt><Super>z` — pop: undo (remove the newest Nexus item).
- `import`/`enqueue`/`run-next`/`drain` — available as unbound templates.
- HUD `Enter` — explicit export of the selected item; `Ctrl+Enter` reuses it as a Nexus input.

## Key concepts
- Nexus clipboard = top of `stack.json`. Inference never writes the system clipboard.
- Export is explicit: `copy-top` or HUD Enter/Copiar. Import is explicit: `push-process`/`import`.
- Visual history: searchable tabs (Pilha/Histórico/Fila/Prompts); history.jsonl read newest-first.
- Prompt templates: built-in library, fill a shortcut prompt in prefs or enqueue from the HUD.
- Quiet feedback: successes → transient status chip + history log; system notifications per `notify-level` (default errors only).
- LIFO stack: newest first; results are `kind: "result"` nodes with `parentId` = source.
- FIFO: prompts enqueued as data; `run-next` consumes one per press, `drain` loops; consume only after success.
- Shortcuts: JSON array in GSettings `shortcuts` (`{id,label,accel,mode,prompt}`), mirrored into `hotkey-slot-0..11` for `Main.wm.addKeybinding`; the single Super leader uses `command-accel` → `hotkey-command`.
- Super command bar: St-only modal; resolves configured shortcut by mode, falls back to a synthetic one so all palette keys work without extra global grabs.
- Pure/impure split: logic in pure modules (node --test), GJS/UI thin, GJS smoke + manual validation.
- /v1 contract: POST chat/completions (OpenAI-compatible), SSE streaming with `data: [DONE]` terminator.
- GJS/libsoup3: no promisify on send_and_read_async; send_finish() returns Gio.InputStream; TextDecoder has no stream option.
- State: ~/.local/share/nexus-clip-gnome/{stack.json,fifo.json,history.jsonl} (tree-ready via id/parentId).

## Constraints
- GNOME Shell 45–51 (ESM; no imports.gi legacy). Wayland reload (logout/login) needed after install.
- No GTK in the shell process (freeze risk); prefs run in a separate process.
- No credentials in the repo (api-key via dconf). No providers other than OpenAI-compatible /v1.
